title: Positive quasi-coherent cohomology on inverse affine opens
statement: Let f:X→Y be quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Suppose R^q f_*M=0 for every quasi-coherent module M and integer q>0. For any affine open V⊆Y, any quasi-coherent O_X-module F and p∈ℕ with p>0, the open module cohomology H^p(f⁻¹V,F|f⁻¹V) [def-sc-open-module-cohomology] is zero.

source.place: Tag 08D5 affine localization; Cohomology Tag 01F4 (2), Tags 08FE, 01E1, 01XJ and 01XB

proof.text: Put U=f⁻¹V and g=f|V. Restrict a chosen injective resolution using lem-sc-ringed-space-restrict-injective-resolution and exactness from lem-sc-derived-open-restriction-adjunction-exact. Transport through Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U. The natural section isomorphism on U identifies the sections complexes. Mathlib resolution comparison and exact scalar forgetting yield the private open_cohomology_restrict_iso, identifying the conclusion with the underlying additive group of H^p(U,F|U).

Use homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso (bounded-below/unbounded compatibility plus the single-object comparison) to transfer hacyc in degree p to ordinary R^p f_*F. Prove the ordinary open restriction comparison directly: transport the restricted resolution through overEquiv, use pushforwardComp and pushforwardCongr₂ with image_morphismRestrict_preimage and morphismRestrict_app for the termwise natural comparison f_*⋙restrict V ≅ restrict U⋙g_*, and use exact restriction to commute homology. Thus R^p g_*(F|U) is zero. No derived category on U or V is required.

The restriction G=F|U is quasi-coherent and g is qcqs by Mathlib. Apply the existing Scheme.Modules.isQuasicoherent_higherDirectImage g G q from DirectImage.Sections to obtain clause (1) of lem-pc-finite-support-hi, without its uniform bound. Affine open module vanishing on top of V and moduleCohomology_top_iso make each positive module cohomology H^r(V,R^q g_*G) zero (reflecting zero from the underlying group by ModuleCat.isZero_of_subsingleton).

Apply exists_lerayEdge_isIso_of_vanishing g to the vanishing from the preceding step. In degree p its target is the global sections of R^p g_*G, already zero. Additive global sections and forgetting preserve zero, and IsZero.of_iso transfers this zero through the Leray edge and open_cohomology_restrict_iso to the exact conclusion. The formulas work also for empty opens.

mathlib_searches.query: Positive cohomology of quasi coherent sheaves vanishes on inverse images of affine opens when all positive higher direct images vanish
If higher pushforwards of quasicoherent modules vanish then cohomology of quasicoherent sheaves on inverse images of affine opens vanishes

msearch grep: 0 hits. Local affine-open module vanishing requires the source open itself affine, which need not hold here. LerayDegenerateSections gives the global edge, and restriction interfaces require composition to obtain this consequence. Blueprint search 01F4: no duplicate blueprint node.

lean.statement:
theorem qcoh_acyclic_inverse_affine_open_vanishing {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wY} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (hacyc : ∀ (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)),
      F.IsQuasicoherent → ∀ (p : ℤ), 0 < p →
        IsZero ((schemeModuleHigherDirectImage f p).obj F))
    (V : Y.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent) (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero ((RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p (f ⁻¹ᵁ V)).obj F)
